claire: Quick note from the reranker bring-up: I A/B'd the new ranker-v2 (PTQ int8) using a compact "prefixed" prompt (we call it 'norm-prefix') vs no-prefix. Results are split by corpus; ndcg improves on doc-knowledge corpora but mrr regresses on short support queries. Need eyes.

devon: paste numbers? small sample or full holdout?

claire: small exploratory run: holdout=2026-04-02 stratified intents, samples=5000, seed=11. snapshot below.

mike: table paste:

```
corpus       | arm        | ndcg@10 | mrr
-------------|------------|---------|------
kb_facts     | no-prefix  | 0.721   | 0.481
kb_facts     | norm-prefix| 0.735   | 0.477
support_logs | no-prefix  | 0.663   | 0.406
support_logs | norm-prefix| 0.652   | 0.389
```

claire: Diagnostics: emitted per-query token diffs and tie-rate. norm-prefix sometimes causes the tokenizer to merge prefix with first word if punctuation absent, shifting subword boundaries. PTQ appears to amplify tiny score deltas (score-gap std rises). Also, support docs often contain HTML/inline code which interacts with candidate truncation.

devon: any reproducible example?

claire: example token diff: raw query "resetpassword" -> tokens [reset, pass, word]; prefixed "NP resetpassword" -> tokens [np, re##set, pass, word] (first token split changed). Top2 score gap reduced from 7e-3 to 1e-4, ordering flips after PTQ.

mike: interesting. try inserting a zero-width space between prefix and query to avoid merges? also compare with --strip-formatting.

claire: already tried two quick variants: (A) punctuation-safe prefix "Query:\n" reduced support MRR loss by ~40% vs raw norm-prefix, (B) zero-width space variant eliminated most token-merge cases but looked hacky. strip-formatting run removed the MRR drop.

devon: plan?

claire: propose full triage matrix and runs:
1) arms: no-prefix, norm-prefix, punct-safe-prefix, zwsp-prefix
2) with/without --strip-formatting
3) PTQ calibrations with seeds [3, 17, 73] to measure quant sensitivity
4) emit per-query: ndcg_delta, mrr_delta, tie_flag, token_shift_index, score_gap_pre/post quant
5) compute effect matrix keyed by (corpus, query_len_bin, html_noise_bin) and a z-score column for significance

mike: good. add deterministic fallback tie-breaker (rank_fallback=doc_hash) as a measurement-only flag so we can quantify tie flipping contribution.

claire: eval command I used for the initial run:
```
./eval/eval_rerank \
  --model models/ranker-v2-int8.ptq \
  --holdout s3://bench/holdouts/2026-04-02.json \
  --priming templates/norm-prefix.json \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 11 --samples 5000 \
  --emit-token-diff --emit-tie-rate --out s3://bench/artifacts/6909876543_initial.json
```

eval-bot: job 6909876550 started: eval_rerank (arms=4, strip-formatting=both, samples=5000).

devon: after runs, let's produce a short recommendation pack: (A) enable punct-safe prefix for KB routes, (B) route support_logs with prefix disabled or strip formatting upstream, or (C) if PTQ instability dominates, consider hybrid quant (mixed-precision) for tie-sensitive workloads. Include per-slice rollout risk.

claire: will run matrix and push artifacts + effect matrix CSV to s3. tagging slices: "short-support", "kb-ambiguous", "html-heavy". posting updates when jobs finish. :hourglass:
